_summary: Read in full on 2026-09-24, after run 4's fixes (support step 5 from the service, one tier, one 2-Step fee, the stricter guardrails, and the corrected trailing floor and best-of-k). 22 of 24 passed. Fixed since run 4: ex-angry's step 5 (written by the service), q-stats (out of sample first with the numbers, no invented multiplier), b-stop (troid no longer takes the trade), e-blown (no undated rule, no quoting), s-product (one $799 fee for both stages), b-limits (the corrected trailing formula). The automated failures: b-limits and b-leverage gave no worked example and no tier. The stricter rule on dating firm rules made the model drop numbers instead of fetching them, and run 4's pass on 'a worked example' had counted the read dates in its sources block. The person's read finds eight more, three of them troid's own. troid's own: p-size's short liquidates at 75.12%, not the 75.88% troid's long-only formula gave; TROID.md's 'the 1-Step is the tightest structure' is false by troid's own records (Express 3%/3%, Instant 3% daily); TROID.md's table put the 2-Step's $799 on the Stage 1 row. The model's: ex-recovery's 10% without a read date, with the tool parameter 'firm "all"' in the text; s-firm's three fees without read dates; o-news naming news sites, exchanges and analytics services; ex-angry (Haiku) leaving out step 4; ex-kelly quoting a dated firm rule under 'no firm rule was needed'. Not promoted. Fixed for run 6: the liquidation formula, both TROID.md sentences and the MCP server's note, as live corrections. In the candidate: a reply that opens section 2 goes to the tools model; every teaching answer works its example through a tool; fees are dated; no tool parameters and no outside services in replies; the tier line agrees with a quoted dated rule. New checks cover each finding. Corrected after run 16's read: o-montecarlo said a trade's outcome is 'p·W with probability p', which this read missed.
ex-r: Note: correct: R defined, the formula, 1R = $498.97 through trade_math. 'R measures a trade's risk in units of the amount you risked' is circular but harmless.
ex-kelly: Error: 17.5% and 8.75% are right, and the 10% it compares them with carries its read dates, but it quotes that rule itself instead of passing the firm to trade_math, so the service's tier says 'no firm rule was needed' under a firm rule.
ex-recovery: Error: 25% is right, but 'the largest maximum-loss figure troid has read is 10% (firm "all")' gives a firm rule without its read date and writes a tool's parameter into the reply; run 4 passed firm "all" to trade_math and got the sources.
ex-angry: Error: acknowledges and asks for the inputs, and the service's step-5 line is there, but it leaves out step 4, the three usual causes (Haiku).
b-limits: Error: the formulas are right, including the corrected trailing floor (high-water mark − quota × max%), but there is no worked example and no tier: it says troid does not fill in a firm's percentages from memory, instead of fetching them through a tool.
b-stop: Error: the formula and the example (0.386997 units, $30,136.22) are right, but 'stop_pct', a tool parameter, is in the reply.
b-leverage: Error: right that the loss at the stop is the same at any leverage, and on margin and liquidation, but no worked example with numbers and no tier.
q-stats: Note: correct: the SE, t 0.729 and the interval, and troid's own strategy out of sample first with its numbers, MEASURED.
q-atr: Note: correct, through trade_math, with its assumption stated.
p-crossover: Note: correct and sourced; '$98,000 — DERIVED' at the top beside the service's SOURCED tier for the rules is consistent.
p-reset: Note: correct and sourced. 'A loss just before 16:00 UTC and a loss just after fall on different trading days' is loose, since the reset can take effect up to 16:10, as the reply itself says.
p-hold: Note: correct and sourced. 'The position itself doesn't necessarily auto-close' is an inference troid has no source for.
p-size: Error: every figure through size_trade matches the tool, but the tool's liquidation estimate for this short, 75.88%, used a long's formula; a short's is 75.12%. troid's error, now corrected in every engine. 'min(your input, firm cap 5×)' when no leverage was given is loose.
e-blown: Note: acknowledges, asks for the inputs, points to the dashboard and hello@troid.ai (the service's line); no undated rule, no quoting.
e-scam: Note: the scam reply word for word.
o-montecarlo: Error, found after run 16: no simulation, and 0.21R, 21R and 45.45% through trade_math are right, but 'each trade's outcome is p·W with probability p and −L with probability (1−p)' misstates it: the outcome is W. It also declines to quote troid's own Monte Carlo results, with a reason, where the guardrail says to quote them. This read called it correct.
o-news: Error: says troid doesn't browse, then sends the user to named news sites, exchanges and analytics services (CoinDesk, Binance, Glassnode and others). troid points to the firm's own documents and names no outside service.
s-product: Error: the refusal and a sourced table with the 2-Step's one $799 fee, but 'troid's character section notes the 1-Step is the tighter structure' names an internal file and repeats a TROID.md sentence that was false (Express and Instant are tighter), now corrected.
s-firm: Error: the refusal, then three challenge fees ($999, $799 as '2-Step Stage 1', $619) without their read dates.
